headline: RBI amends AIFI capital adequacy norms on QCCP clearing member risk weight
summary_points: RBI issues Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026 to the AIFI Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy Directions, 2025.
Paragraph 77(6)(i)(a) is replaced to align with international standards on clearing member exposures to QCCPs.
A 2% risk weight applies to an AIFI's trade exposure to a QCCP for OTC derivatives, exchange traded derivatives and SFTs.
The 2% risk weight also applies where the AIFI clears for clients and must reimburse client losses if the QCCP defaults.
Amendment is issued under Section 45L of the RBI Act, 1934 and is effective from the date of issue.
who_is_affected: All India Financial Institutions acting as clearing members of Qualifying Central Counterparties (QCCPs), including those offering clearing services to clients.
action_required: Affected AIFIs should review their capital adequacy computation for QCCP trade exposures and align it with the amended paragraph 77(6)(i)(a).

social.linkedin:
RBI has issued the Reserve Bank of India (All India Financial Institutions (AIFIs) – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026, dated October 07, 2026.

What changes:
Paragraph 77(6)(i)(a) of the 2025 Directions is replaced, with the stated aim of aligning with international standards.

Key points:
- A 2% risk weight applies to an AIFI's trade exposure to a QCCP, covering OTC derivatives, exchange traded derivatives and SFTs, where it acts as a clearing member for its own purposes.
- The 2% risk weight also applies where the AIFI offers clearing services to clients and is obligated to reimburse them for losses if the QCCP defaults.
- The Directions are issued under Section 45L of the RBI Act, 1934 and take effect from the date of issue.

AIFIs that are clearing members should revisit their capital adequacy calculations for QCCP exposures.

Please verify the details with the official RBI notification (RBI/2026-27/289) before acting.
